nodes.label: AI agents can now attempt complex real-world tasks, but the ecosystem is fragmented
Software is the most powerful human interface with the world; agents acting through software can scale human productivity
Existing frameworks (AutoGPT, LangChain, MetaGPT, AutoGen, SWE-Agent) each address subsets of the problem; no unified platform exists
No open platform combines: safe sandboxed execution, extensible skills, multi-agent delegation, and multi-benchmark evaluation for generalist agents
Can a unified platform enable development and evaluation of generalist agents that act through software?
OpenHands: event-stream architecture + Docker sandbox + AgentSkills + multi-agent + 15-benchmark evaluation
CodeActAgent as generalist baseline; 15 benchmarks spanning 3 categories; 0-shot evaluation without hint text
CodeActAgent achieves 26.0% SWE-Bench Lite (claude-3-5-sonnet), competitive with open-source specialists
CodeActAgent fixes 79.3% of HumanEvalFix bugs (0-shot), nearly doubling non-agentic baselines
BrowsingAgent achieves 15.5% on WebArena, competitive with domain-general LLM agents
CodeActAgent surpasses GPT-4 CoT on GPQA (52% vs 38.8%) and exceeds task-specific baselines on AgentBench and MINT
One generalist agent achieves competitive performance across all three task categories without modification
Code as an action space is sufficiently expressive to handle software, web, and reasoning tasks; platform infrastructure accelerates this research
OpenHands: open platform + generalist evaluation + community ecosystem; MIT licensed
No variance estimates; struggles with long files; workflow generation still manual
Open platforms that unify evaluation are necessary infrastructure for agent research; software-action agents generalize more than expected
Stronger training, multi-modality, automated workflow, improved file editing
